description: FIRELENS is a project focused on making satellite-based active fire data more understandable and accessible. We explore MODIS and VIIRS detections to identify historical patterns and visualize fire activity across Indonesian regions. We welcome passionate collaborators interested in Earth science, data analysis, coding, web development, and data visualization who want to create meaningful solutions together.
summary:
FIRELENS is an interactive web-based platform designed to make satellite-based active fire data more understandable and accessible. Using 12,809 historical fire detection records from NASA FIRMS, collected by MODIS and VIIRS sensors between August and October 2024, the project explores fire activity patterns across Riau and Central Kalimantan, Indonesia.

The platform transforms complex satellite datasets into interactive maps, visualizations, and statistical summaries. It provides a Public Mode for general audiences and a Research Mode for users who want to explore the data through filters, geographic analysis, Fire Radiative Power (FRP) statistics, and data exports.

FIRELENS supports the challenge of understanding historical fire patterns from MODIS and VIIRS observations by presenting their detection records in a more accessible format. It also highlights the importance of interpreting satellite observations responsibly, recognizing sensor differences and data limitations. Ultimately, FIRELENS aims to bridge the gap between complex Earth observation data and public understanding.
details:
FIRELENS is an interactive web-based platform that makes historical satellite active-fire detection data easier to explore, understand, and communicate. It uses 12,809 records from NASA's Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS), covering MODIS and VIIRS observations across Riau and Central Kalimantan, Indonesia, from August 1 to October 31, 2024.

The platform processes and presents the data through interactive maps, monthly visualizations, statistical summaries, geographic filters, and downloadable datasets. It offers two experiences: Public Mode, which provides accessible explanations and visual summaries for general audiences, and Research Mode, which supports deeper exploration through filters, geographic analysis, and Fire Radiative Power (FRP) statistics.

FIRELENS helps users identify historical patterns and understand how satellite detection records are distributed across regions, months, and sensors. Its creative approach combines data exploration with an accessible interface and a friendly visual identity, making complex Earth observation information less intimidating.

The project was developed using Python and Streamlit, with data processing and visualization libraries used to organize and present the dataset. Important considerations included data quality, differences between MODIS and VIIRS observations, responsible interpretation, and the distinction between satellite detection records and unique fire events.

FIRELENS aims to improve public understanding of satellite fire data and encourage informed exploration of historical fire activity. It is an exploratory research and visualization platform, not a real-time fire alert system.
